newsitem.title: USA: Missouri corn harvest ahead of average pace.
newsitem.headline: Missouri corn harvest ahead of average pace.

text.p: Missouri's corn crop was harvested on 45 percent of the acreage, slightly ahead of the five-year average of 40 percent and last year's 32 percent, according to the Missouri Agricultural Statistics Service.

"Favorable reports of early corn yields have been common," the report said. "The most favorable ratings are found in the northwestern, north-central, west-central, southwestern and southeastern districts."
Nearly all the crop has been harvested across the southern third of the state, about 45 percent across the central third and 30 percent across the northern third.
Soybeans were 11 percent harvested, up from last year's eight percent but still behind the average of 17 percent.
Thirty-five percent were mature, up from last year's 30 percent but down from the normal 50 percent.
Soybean ratings were little changed from a week earlier with 57 percent good to excellent.
Winter wheat was 17 percent seeded, down from last year's 19 percent and the average pace of 18 percent. Five percent had emerged, versus last year's four percent and the normal six percent.
